method: Claude's rating: crowd score weighted by review volume, plus awards and guide listings, spread onto a 5-star scale. An experiment; compare with your own.

days.5: Bar food 12:00–21:00; restaurant dinner in the evening
days.6: Bar food 12:00–21:00; restaurant dinner in the evening

google: The Lakeside Hotel and Leisure Centre
venues.name: Lakeside Hotel (Cois Lacha)
venues.note: Hotel bar and restaurant on Ballina quay with river views. Reviewers praise the bar food, friendly service and the breakfast. O'Hara's Bar serves food daily; the restaurant opens Friday and Saturday evenings and for Sunday lunch. Taste of the Waterways award 2022.

venues.name: Killaloe Hotel & Spa
venues.note: Hotel dining at Kincora Harbour, a 20-minute walk from the town. Reviewers mention a warm welcome, generous portions and well-presented plates. Food is served in O'Brien's Bar & Restaurant; book by phone.

venues.name: Bridge 14 Coffee
venues.note: Café and bakery for brunch and lunch. Known for its home-made pastries (cinnamon buns, maritozzo), Turkish eggs and good coffee; cosy, friendly room.

venues.name: Flanagan's on the Lake
venues.note: Big, lively lakeside bar-restaurant with outdoor tables. Mid-priced menu: seafood, duck, sea bass, burgers, with vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options; good with children and groups. On busy days expect a queue and slow service. Hours not on its own site; ring ahead.

venues.name: Bless Cafe
venues.note: Cosy café in the Convent Hill shopping centre: breakfasts, plenty of gluten-free choice and muffins baked daily; quirky collectible decor and very friendly staff. Hours not on its own site; ring ahead.

venues.name: RAW Café & Pizzeria
venues.note: Quirky café and pizzeria in an interiors shop, with art for sale. Pizza, squid and monkfish curry are the dishes reviewers name; food reviews are mixed. One reviewer found live jazz on a Sunday evening. The tourism listing says the café is temporarily closed for refurbishment.

venues.name: Canton House
venues.note: Chinese takeaway and restaurant. Quick service; reviews of the food are mixed.

venues.name: Ponte Vecchio
venues.note: Quirky Italian deli, wine bar and second-hand bookshop with nooks to hide in. Thin-based pizzas, Italian coffee and cakes, affogato, and Italian wine and groceries to take away; food reviews are mixed, the coffee is well liked. In Waterways Ireland's food guide. Hours not on its own site; ring ahead.

venues.name: Tuscany Bistro
venues.note: Italian bistro, good for an occasion. Reviewers praise fresh cooking, the bruschetta and cannoli, and friendly staff who will adapt dishes for vegetarian and gluten-free diets. In Waterways Ireland's food guide. Closed Monday to Thursday.

google: Brian Boru on the Hill, Bar, Restaurant, Event Centre & Off Licence
venues.name: Brian Boru on the Hill
venues.note: Pub and restaurant up the hill in Ballina: a cosy locals' favourite with a welcoming owner and staff. Hearty pub food and weekend specials: seafood chowder with brown bread, bangers and mash, crispy pork belly, chicken liver pâté, home-made apple pie and cheesecakes. Its own Instagram page gives food Friday 16:00–21:00, Saturday 14:00–21:00 and Sunday 12:30–20:00 (bank holiday Monday 13:00–20:00); ring to check the kitchen is open.

venues.name: Goosers Bar & Eating House
venues.note: Cosy thatched-style pub and eating house in Ballina, with outdoor tables; a favourite after the Ballycuggeran walks. Hearty, well-cooked pub food: seafood specials, fish and chips, duck and fillet steak; gluten-free catered for. Service gets mixed reviews. In Waterways Ireland's food guide. Open seven days from 12:00; lunch from 12:30 and dinner from 18:00, end times not stated.

venues.name: Liam O'Riain's Bar
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food. Classic friendly local on Ballina's Main Street with river views, a well-kept pint and trad sessions (one reviewer found music on a Tuesday from 21:00); welcoming to boaters.

venues.name: West Lake Coffee
venues.note: Coffee hatch by the lake at Ballycuggeran with benches out the back. Known for ice-cream sundaes, açaí bowls, pizza slices and coffee; order at one window, collect at the other. Its own Instagram page says open daily 08:30–18:00, which differs from the hours shown here; ring ahead.

venues.name: McNamara's Bar & Bistro
venues.note: Bar and bistro in the middle of Scarriff serving proper Irish pub grub (its own Facebook) from a large menu with plenty of daily specials. Reviewers single out friendly, unhurried service and fair prices for food and drink. Hours not on its own site; ring ahead.

venues.name: Sweet Home Cafe
venues.note: Small family-run café on Market Square: excellent coffee (Anam, roasted in the Burren), sausage rolls, toasted sandwiches, waffles and milkshakes, with daily specials such as a slow-cooked brisket melt or chicken tikka wrap, and a soup-and-sandwich deal (€8 in October 2026, its own Instagram). Warm welcome.

venues.name: Nuala's, Tuamgraney
venues.note: Family-run pub dating from 1850, cosy inside, with good-value home cooking: seafood chowder, fish and chips, beef stew, roast turkey, soup with brown bread and generous veg; its Instagram bio also offers takeaway food daily 12:00–20:00. Service can be slow when busy. Trad music at weekends; breakfast 10:00–12:30 Mon–Sat, lunch until 16:30 and à la carte until 21:00. In Waterways Ireland's food guide.

venues.name: Boat House Cafe
venues.note: Seasonal coffee and ice-cream hut at the harbour by the Blue Flag beach: coffee, Mullins ice cream, sundaes and açaí bowls; no meals. Its own Instagram said weekends only until the end of September 2026, and it closed for the winter in October 2025, so expect it shut out of season. The hours shown here look wrong.

venues.name: That's My Brew
venues.note: Takeaway café and coffee roaster on Main Street with a small garden: some of the best coffee in the area, a best-selling chocolate brownie, cookies and croissants, and a shop of art and gifts. No meals described.

venues.name: Seasons Restaurant
venues.note: Relaxed, family-friendly restaurant on Main Street, good for children; generous plates of pasta, pizza and fish and chips at modest prices, though cooking is uneven when busy. Shares a phone number with The River Run. Hours not on its own site; ring ahead.

google: The River Run Bar and restaurant
venues.name: The River Run
venues.note: Family-run village pub and restaurant overlooking Lough Derg: welcoming locals and comfort food. Roast beef is the dish reviewers praise; its own Instagram shows beef and Guinness pie, a fish burger and cheese-stuffed panko chicken among the specials, plus pizza and burgers.

venues.name: Berrytree Café
venues.note: Bright, carefully run café and bakery, shortlisted for National Café of the Year 2025 (its own Instagram): home baking (pear and almond cake, scones, sausage rolls, vegan cakes), excellent coffee, wine and well-made sandwiches such as the Normandy bap. Very friendly; handles groups. Open until Christmas, with a winter break in January and February. Open 11:00–17:00 Thursday to Sunday, and Wednesday to Sunday in June to August.

venues.name: Larkins
venues.note: Traditional thatched pub by the harbour that has become mainly a restaurant, long a boaters' stop. Famous for its seafood chowder; also roast of the day, steaks and lemon meringue pie. Prices have crept up; fills up, so book. Open Thursday to Sunday from 12:00, closed Monday to Wednesday; kitchen times not stated. In Waterways Ireland's food guide.

venues.name: Lough Derg House & Lake Café
venues.note: Guesthouse on the harbour with a host much praised for his welcome and breakfasts; the reviews are of the B&B, not the café. Taste of the Waterways award 2022 (lake café). Whether the café is open now is not known; ring ahead.

venues.name: The Baker's Table
venues.note: Weekend coffee shop by the harbour: very good coffee, home-made sweet bakes and snacks.

venues.name: The Whiskey Still
venues.note: Authentic, homely pub-restaurant beside the marina, the only one in Dromineer. Fresh home-cooked food in generous portions: pork belly, halibut and other fish specials, organic chicken, fish and chips. Friendly owner and staff; book in summer. Trad sessions some nights. Its own Instagram (1 Sep 2026) gives winter hours: Wednesday to Friday from 17:00, Saturday and Sunday from 15:00, which differs from the hours shown here.

venues.name: The Derg Inn
venues.note: Warm, recently renovated village pub-restaurant with a fire and a beer garden inside a historic bawn wall. Big portions of hearty food: ribeye, steak sandwich, fish and chips, duck wings; the kitchen uses local seasonal produce, game and Atlantic fish. Busy at weekends. Live music. In Waterways Ireland's food guide. Hours and menus not on its own site; ring ahead.

venues.name: Paddy's Bar
venues.note: Cosy, spacious bar a short walk from Terryglass Quay, run by the Tierney family since 2006. Big portions of good pub food: chicken curry, beef and Guinness stew, fish specials, Sunday roasts; not cheap but worth it. Bar food served all day.

google: Portumna Castle Tea Room - CaToCa Fine Food
venues.name: Portumna Castle Tea Room
venues.note: Tea room in the castle's old coach house, on the forest walk to the harbour, with an art gallery upstairs. Home baking, salads and quiche, good coffee, with gluten-free and vegan options; some reviewers found the counter service abrupt. Dogs outside only. Open daily from March to October.

venues.name: Modena Restaurant
venues.note: Indian and Italian menus under one roof, also a coffee and wine bar; homely, family-friendly. Reviewers rate the Indian food well (butter chicken, tandoori fish) and Malaysian dishes are cooked on request. Lots of gluten-free choice; covered outdoor area where dogs are welcome. All-day breakfast; hours not on its own site.

venues.name: Roma Take Away Restaurant
venues.note: Family-run Italian takeaway and restaurant, quick and friendly. Big menu of pizza, chicken and fresh-cut chips, fish and chips and doner; good value.

venues.name: Spice n Rice
venues.note: Indian restaurant and takeaway, plain to look at but well reviewed: curries made fresh, naan, steaks, doner kebabs, burgers and pasta for children. Generous portions at fair prices; friendly staff.

venues.name: Beehive Pizzeria
venues.note: Tiny, homely restaurant where the owner cooks in view: thin-crust pizza and home-made pasta that an Italian reviewer rated, at reasonable prices. Cash only, reviewers say. In Waterways Ireland's food guide. Hours not published online; ring ahead.

venues.name: Cafe Rose
venues.note: Friendly town café for breakfast, lunch, coffee and cake; good coffee and wholesome food, though one reviewer found the full Irish poor.

venues.name: The Courtyard Café Portumna
venues.note: Café in the old courthouse on Main Street with a big dog-friendly courtyard out the back. Local ingredients: toasties, sourdough, bagels, açaí bowls, home-made cakes and weekly specials (soup, tuna melt, lasagne), with speciality coffee. Very friendly owner and staff. Its own Instagram says open Sundays 10:00–14:00.

venues.name: Cool Beanz Café
venues.note: Small, dog-friendly coffee shop for breakfasts, toasties and treats, with organic options, gluten-free baking and grain salads; picnics made up to take away (its own Instagram). Reviews are split: some praise the coffee and staff, others found it bland and overpriced.

venues.name: Bethlehem Restaurant
venues.note: Takeaway with a spacious, clean sit-in room: fish and chips, kebabs, pizza and subs in big portions at low prices; fast, friendly service. Boaters recommend it after a wet day on the lake.

venues.name: The Boathouse Bar
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food. Warm, welcoming bar with a big beer garden out the back, sport on many screens, a pool table and some live music.

venues.name: Curley's Bar
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food. Charming, spotless traditional country pub with a friendly owner and locals, a well-poured pint, live music and a garden.
